post.title: FHA vs conventional: the fee that never cancels
post.ig:
Put under 10% down on an FHA loan and the mortgage insurance never cancels on its own.
FHA: 3.5% down with a 580+ score, 1.75% upfront premium, about 0.55% a year on most loans (HUD rules, 2026).
Our math: $350,000 home, 3.5% down = $337,750 loan, $5,911 upfront and about $155 a month in year one.
Conventional: 3% down possible; PMI runs 0.2% to 2% a year (Fannie Mae) and must end at 22% equity by law.
Sources: HUD, FHFA, Fannie Mae, CFPB.
